sections.heading: C — Pavement markings: line types, word and symbol markings, stop and yield lines, bike lanes and crosswalks
sections.markdown:
## C — Pavement markings: line types, word and symbol markings, stop and yield lines, bike lanes and crosswalks

FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A24
Pavement markings are lines painted on the road that guide and inform you without making you take your eyes off the roadway. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A24
In some places lines are made extra wide or fitted with reflective markers so they catch your attention and are easier to see. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A24
A single broken white line divides lanes carrying traffic the same way on roads with more than one lane, and you may cross it to change lanes. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A24
A single broken yellow line divides traffic moving in opposite directions and allows careful passing from either side; it serves as the center line on 2-lane, 2-way roads. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A24
A single solid white line marks the right edge of the road and can also divide same-direction lanes where changing lanes is discouraged. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A24
A single solid yellow line marks the left edge of divided highways, one-way roads and ramps. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A24
A divided highway is one with a guardrail, a strip of land or some other barrier between the two directions of traffic. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A24
Double broken yellow lines side by side mark the edges of a reversible lane, and you enter or leave that lane only as its signs and signals permit. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A24
Double solid white lines side by side divide same-direction lanes where lane changes are not allowed. [A24]
Why it matters: a single solid white line only discourages a lane change; double solid white forbids it.
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A24
Double solid white lines may also set general lanes apart from HOV lanes, or appear ahead of an obstruction you are allowed to pass on either side. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A24
Double solid yellow lines divide opposing traffic and forbid passing from either direction. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A24
You are allowed to turn left across double solid yellow lines, for example to pull into a driveway. [A24]
Why it matters: double solid yellow bans passing, not left turns.
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A24
A solid yellow line beside a broken yellow line is used on two-way roads where passing is allowed in only one direction. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A24
With a solid-plus-broken yellow pair, drivers on the broken-line side may pass carefully, while drivers on the solid-line side may not pass. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F15 | anchor: A24
Solid-plus-broken yellow lines also outline a two-way left turn lane, with the solid lines on the outside and the broken lines on the inside. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F16 | anchor: A24
Single dotted lines in yellow or white carry lane lines through an intersection, and drivers there should keep inside those markings. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F17 | anchor: A25
Word and symbol markings on the pavement tell you how to use a lane, which direction to travel, and when a lane reduction is coming, such as two lanes narrowing to one. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-F18 | anchor: A25
Arrows and other word messages painted in a lane show how you are allowed to move from that lane. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-F19 | anchor: A25
SCHOOL and RxR painted on the road warn that you are nearing a school area or a railroad crossing. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-F20 | anchor: A25
A stop line is a solid white line showing where you must stop for a STOP sign or a red traffic signal. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-F21 | anchor: A25
Yield lines are rows of small triangles painted across a lane that show where you must yield to vehicles or pedestrians. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-F22 | anchor: A25
Most Maryland roads that bicycles share with motor vehicles carry no special signs or pavement markings for bicycles. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-F23 | anchor: A25
Shared-use lane markings, found mostly in cities, warn drivers that cyclists may be present, show cyclists where to ride, and discourage riding against traffic. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-F24 | anchor: A25
Bicycle-only lanes are separated from motor vehicle lanes by solid or broken white lines and may be marked with bike lane signs or bicycle symbols and arrows. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-F25 | anchor: A25
Where parallel parking is permitted, similar lines may separate a bike lane from the parking lane. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-F26 | anchor: A25
Crosswalk lines are solid white lines marking where pedestrians cross, and some crosswalks add lines between them or use other lines instead. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-F27 | anchor: A26
Citing the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, the manual says a crash where the limit is 65 mph or more is over twice as likely to be fatal as one where the limit is 45 or 50 mph. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-F28 | anchor: A26
The same NHTSA comparison says a crash on a road posted at 65 mph or more is nearly 5 times as likely to be fatal as one on a road posted at 40 mph or less. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-F29 | anchor: A26
According to the manual, no single step does more to keep you from being killed or badly hurt in a crash than wearing a seat belt, on every trip and in front or back seats. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-F30 | anchor: A26
About 90 percent of Maryland drivers and passengers buckle up, and the state's stated goal is 100 percent. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-F31 | anchor: A26
Buckling up takes about 3 seconds, and the manual says most injuries and deaths among unbelted crash victims could have been avoided by wearing a belt. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0026]

Glossary: broken line — a dashed line you may cross when it is safe [A24]. Reversible lane — a lane whose direction of travel changes at different times [A24]. Stop line — the solid white line marking where to stop [A25]. Yield line — a row of small painted triangles marking where to yield [A25]. Shared-use lane marking — a pavement marking showing that bicycles and vehicles share the lane [A25].
Memory aid: yellow lines separate opposite directions, white lines separate the same direction; broken means you may cross, solid means stay put [A24].
Misconception: double solid yellow lines do not ban every crossing; you may still turn left across them into a driveway [A24].

items.why: each passing and lane-change rule depends on the color and pattern of a painted line, so learners need picture-based road-view drills rather than text-only cards
